t: Row With Maximum Ones — Single Scan
o: Scan each row, count its ones, and keep the first row achieving the strict maximum (strict comparison automatically keeps the smallest index on ties). Example 1: both rows have one 1, row 0 wins. Example 2/3: row 1 has more ones. With m,n ≤ 100, any direct approach works.
k: Strict '>' comparison when updating the best guarantees the smallest row index wins ties.

a.n: Approach 1: Linear scan with strict improvement
a.i: Iterate rows, sum each (or count during iteration), and replace the answer only when the count strictly exceeds the current best.
s: For each row compute the ones count; update on strictly greater.

w: Trivial; the only subtlety is tie handling, solved by strict comparison. Follow-up: rows sorted, use binary search per row for O(m log n); or streaming matrices where you cannot revisit rows.
